sections.title: Molecular profile of sex cord–stromal tumours
sections.intro: SCST is **three molecular diseases** that share a morphological family. **AGCT** is defined by the somatic FOXL2 c.402C>G (p.C134W) mutation, with TERT promoter mutation enriched at recurrence [16,17]. **SLCT** is driven by DICER1 RNase IIIb hotspot mutations, about half with a germline DICER1 variant, plus a smaller FOXL2-mutant group in older women [18,19,20]. **JGCT** carries AKT1 in-frame duplications (and GNAS mutations in an earlier study by the same group), but not FOXL2 [21,22]. None of these alterations selects an approved drug; the only treatment-selecting marker in current use is ER/PR for endocrine therapy. **Pathology in brief:** SLCT behaviour tracks stage and differentiation (all well-differentiated tumours benign; 11% of intermediate, 59% of poorly differentiated and 19% of heterologous tumours malignant) [23], and mesenchymal heterologous elements carry most of the stage I recurrence risk [20]. In JGCT, all recurrences with a known mitotic index had >19 mitoses/10 HPF at diagnosis [24]. Inhibin B and AMH are the AGCT follow-up markers (AUC 0.94 and 0.92; the combination detects recurrence better than inhibin B alone) [25], but inhibin was ≤10 pg/mL in 40% of patients with measurable recurrent stromal tumours in GOG-0187 [26].

notes.title: Practical consequence for testing
notes.md:
1. **FOXL2 C134W confirms AGCT.** A FOXL2-mutant "juvenile" tumour should be reviewed (2/50 were reclassified as AGCT) [22], and a FOXL2-mutant "SLCT" is a distinct older-patient subtype [19].
2. **DICER1 testing in SLCT, gynandroblastoma and JGCT has family consequences.** Germline DICER1 was found in 58% of tested SLCT [20]; three children of women with SLCT were diagnosed with type I pleuropulmonary blastoma through genetic testing and screening, treated by surgery alone [7].
3. **ER/PR IHC is the only test that opens a trial-tested option** (PARAGON, ≥10%) [14], but prospective objective response rates to endocrine therapy were 0–10.5% (Table 3B).
4. **MMR, PD-L1, HRD, HER2 and FRα do not open trial-proven options in SCST** [27].

notes.title: Reading Table 1
notes.md:
- **No randomized adjuvant trial exists in any SCST histotype.** The only protocol-allocated comparison is paediatric TGM-95: no relapses in 11 children with rupture and/or malignant ascites given chemotherapy, 4/4 relapses without it [34].
- **Stage IC GCT: no dataset shows benefit.** NCDB OS HR 1.07 (0.52–2.21), SEER adult GCT DSS 97% vs 94% (P=0.491), meta-analysis pooling adult and juvenile GCT mortality OR 0.83 (0.44–1.57) [15,28,43]. In the whole SEER stage I–III cohort, DSS was lower with chemotherapy (88.8% vs 96.7%), a stage-selection effect [28]. Incomplete surgical staging is the consistent adverse factor (recurrence HR 3.883; death HR 1.84) [40,41].
- **SLCT: the risk sits in differentiation and mesenchymal heterologous elements**, not stage alone [20,23,38]. In the registry, chemotherapy appeared to neutralise the heterologous-element risk (HR 74.18 without vs 1.21 with chemotherapy), but the analysis is unadjusted [20].
- **JGCT: stage ≥IC2 and mitotic index >19/10 HPF mark the high-risk group** [24]; stage I JGCT had no recurrences after fertility-sparing surgery in MITO-9 [42].

notes.title: Traps in Table 2
notes.md:
1. **GOG-0264 did not show that paclitaxel–carboplatin is non-inferior to BEP.** The futility HR of 1.11 (0.57–2.13) rests on 21 and 16 PFS events by arm; median PFS favoured paclitaxel–carboplatin numerically (27.7 vs 19.7 months), response favoured BEP (50% vs 18% of 23 measurable patients), and toxicity favoured paclitaxel–carboplatin [1]. The authors conclude both regimens may be considered.
2. **GOG-0264 says nothing about SLCT**: 3 patients, all on BEP [1].
3. **High response rates in small BEP/PVB series (52–90%) did not translate into durable control**: 1 of 7 metastatic patients in durable remission [44]; 4-year EFS 30% [47]. Under strict RECIST in a referral cohort, response was 22% [48].
4. **Paediatric JGCT evidence is registry-based** (7 stage ≥II patients, 6 alive) [49]; paediatric protocols use cisplatin-based three-drug regimens such as VIP [34].

notes.title: BEP and paclitaxel–carboplatin schedules vs NTUH templates
notes.md:
- **GOG-115 and GOG-0264 BEP (5-day): bleomycin 20 units/m² D1 + etoposide 75 mg/m² D1–5 + cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, q21d ×4** [1,3].
- **GERM CELL TUMOR Bleomycin, Etoposide and Cisplatin (BEP)** (NTUH) is a **3-day** schedule: cisplatin 100 mg/m² D1, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–3, bleomycin 15 mg/m² over 24 h D1–3, 21-day course, 4 courses. This is closest to the MD Anderson SCST schedule (bleomycin 10–15 **mg/day** continuous infusion D1–3, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–3, cisplatin 100 mg/m² D1), which gave 83% response but durable remission in 1 of 7 metastatic patients [44]. It is not the schedule tested in GOG-115 or GOG-0264. Note the bleomycin unit difference (mg/m² vs mg/day).
- **GOG-0264 paclitaxel–carboplatin: paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 6, q21d ×6** [1]. OV Paclitaxel and Carboplatin uses paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5, 6 courses.
- **VIP** (TGM-95 paediatric) has no NTUH template [34].

sections.title: 3. Recurrent disease
sections.intro: Table 3 is split by **therapy class**, not by platinum sensitivity. **3A** = cytotoxic chemotherapy, bevacizumab and secondary cytoreduction. **3B** = endocrine, targeted and immunotherapy. Every row carries a `Prior systemic therapy` column.

notes.title: Why this split exists
notes.md: SCST trials rarely report a platinum-free interval; ALIENOR is the exception, stratifying by <12 vs ≥12 months (72% ≥12 months) [2]. The real decision at relapse is between repeat surgery, chemotherapy and endocrine therapy. Two traps: (1) GOG-0264, GOG-115, EORTC PVB (35 of 38) and the MD Anderson BEP study enrolled **chemotherapy-naive** recurrences, so their response rates are first-chemotherapy results, not salvage-line expectations [1,3,44,45]; (2) endocrine trials report clinical benefit rates that an indolent tumour can reach without drug effect [14].

notes.title: Reading notes for Table 3
notes.md:
- **Weekly paclitaxel is the only randomized reference in relapse** (median PFS 14.7 months). Bevacizumab added response (44% vs 25%) but not 6-month PFR, PFS or OS, and single-agent bevacizumab after progression gave a median PFS of 6.9 months [2]. Single-agent bevacizumab in the GOG trial gave 16.7% partial responses and median PFS 9.3 months [13].
- **Prospective endocrine response rates are low**: anastrozole 10.5%, darolutamide–exemestane–leuprolide 6.25%, and 0% for ketoconazole, orteronel, enzalutamide and onapristone ± anastrozole [14,30,31,32,54,55,56]. The 71% pooled response in case reports [58] is not reproducible. Endocrine therapy is a disease-stabilisation option, not a cytoreductive one.
- **Repeat cytoreduction** carries the largest effect size (OS HR 0.28) but in a surgically selected registry cohort [50]; MITO-9 also found residual tumour at repeat surgery prognostic (5-year OS 55.6% vs 87.4%) [51].
- **Immunotherapy**: 2/8 durable responses with ipilimumab–nivolumab in GCT (1 juvenile-type CR, 1 adult-type PR) [53] vs 0/5 with pembrolizumab [29]; AGCT is MSI-negative and mostly PD-L1-negative [27].
- **LEGRA** (letrozole in GCT) was not found in PubMed on 2026-09-15 and is not tabulated (see Open items).

notes.title: ALIENOR and bevacizumab vs NTUH templates
notes.md:
- **ALIENOR: paclitaxel 80 mg/m² D1, 8, 15 q28d ×6; bevacizumab 10 mg/kg D1 and D15 with chemotherapy, then 15 mg/kg q3w up to 1 year** [2]. There is **no NTUH single-agent weekly paclitaxel template**. OV weekly Paclitaxel and Carboplatin(打三休一) gives the same paclitaxel dose (80 mg/m² D1, 8, 15, 28-day course, 6 courses) but adds carboplatin AUC 2 weekly, which ALIENOR did not test.
- **GOG bevacizumab trial: 15 mg/kg q21d** [13]. OV Avastin is a D1 q21d template with the mg/kg field blank.

notes.title: Reading Table 4
notes.md: The only comparative fertility-sparing result is in AGCT: unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy matched radical surgery (10-year DFS 70% vs 75%), whereas cystectomy did not (16%) [60]. In SLCT, metachronous contralateral tumours occur (4/44 paediatric), and metachronous SLCT occurred in germline DICER1 carriers [7,38], so fertility-sparing surgery needs DICER1-informed surveillance of the remaining ovary. No study tested neoadjuvant chemotherapy against primary surgery in SCST.
